newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X, Indonesian partner in Busang talks.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X, Indonesian partner in Busang talks.

text.p: An Indonesian partner of Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday he had put off a $1.9 billion lawsuit against the mining group because it was willing to discuss the ownership dispute over the Busang gold find.
Businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims to own 40 percent of the spectacular find in East Kalimantan, said Bre-X had been in touch with his lawyers in opening negotiations over their dispute.
He had given Bre-X, which has estimated Busang contains at least 47 million ounces of gold, until December 4 to start serious negotiations.
"I am delaying the legal action because Bre-X has been in touch with my lawyers," he told Reuters.

Merukh, who declined to give further details, had been locked in an ownership dispute with Bre-X, which led to the Indonesian government delaying issuing a contract of work (COW) to Bre-X until their dispute was resolved.
The government has since advised Bre-X to partner Barrick Gold Corp to develop Busang, with Bre-X taking a 25- percent stake and Barrick 75 percent.
It has given both parties until December 4 to strike a deal, and also indicated that it wanted a 10-percent stake to be allocated by Bre-X and Barrick.
Bre-X has a partnership deal with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group, run by President Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto.
Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent stake in Busang's richest parts under the deal.

Barrick has teamed up with a construction company in the Citra Group of Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, in what Barrick had said was a partnership "to prepare us for a potential mining development project".
Warren Beckwith, president of Golden Valley Mines NL of Australia, which has a technical assistance and finance deal with Merukh, confirmed on Monday that Merukh's legal action has been delayed.
"We will hold on (to the lawsuit) since we are having meaningful discussions," he told Reuters.
Beckwith said that the amount of revenue Golden Valley will get from its deal with Merukh will depend on "how things will go when the mine goes into operation".
"The revenue will partly be based on royalties. There are figures in the agreement (with Merukh)," he added.

Beckwith said he was confident that Golden Valley and Merukh would get their share of Busang. "I'm sure the government will take measures to make sure the rights of all parties are protected", he said.
